summary: This section explains how company law offences are handled by courts. It states that most offences are non-cognizable and sets strict rules on who can file a complaint to start a court case. It also exempts certain officials from needing to appear in court personally every time.
points: Every offence under this Act, except those under section 212(6), is treated as non-cognizable.
Courts can only take up an offence if there is a written complaint from the Registrar, a shareholder, a member, or a person authorised by the Central Government.
A person authorised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India can file written complaints for offences related to issuing and transferring securities and unpaid dividends.
A company prosecuting its own officer does not need a complaint from the Registrar or Central Government.
When the Registrar or a Central Government person is the complainant, they do not need to be personally present in court unless the judge specifically asks them to attend.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited noticed that a dividend payment was missed. A person authorised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India filed a written complaint regarding this non-payment of dividend. Meanwhile, Rohan, a shareholder of the company, filed a written complaint about another minor rule violation by an officer. The court accepted these written complaints to begin examining the matters. Later, because the Central Government had authorised a specific officer to file a complaint, that officer did not have to attend every single court hearing in person, as the judge did not demand their personal attendance.

terms.meaning: An offence where police cannot usually arrest a person without a warrant or start an investigation without court permission.
The action taken by a court of law to officially notice and hear a criminal case.
A person appointed to wind up and close down the affairs of a company.

watch: People often confuse who is allowed to file a complaint in court, but the law strictly lists specific authorities and individuals who can do so.
